report_vintage: Retratos da Leitura no Brasil, sixth edition, 2024 national survey
publication_date_basis: Public results presentation date in the primary 28 October event announcement and the publisher-hosted 19 November news item. The 13-11 filename is not treated as publication date.
population: Residents age 5+, including people unable to read
methods: Household face-to-face tablet interviews in 208 municipalities; sample designed using PNADC 2023 population frame.
methods_locator: Printed p.10 and p.12; recent-reader definition printed p.14

visual_validation.status: Rendered and inspected methods, 25 genre categories and 2024 audiobook Yes donut against Firecrawl extraction and web PDF text.

audiobook_question: P71A, ever listened to an audiobook; no bounded recall
genre_question: P37, types read in the last year in paper or digital; eligible base read at least one book in whole or in part in the last three months

added_audiobook_observations.population: Brazil residents age 5+, including people unable to read; national household sample
added_audiobook_observations.period: Lifetime: ever listened to an audiobook
added_audiobook_observations.evidence_locator: Printed p.107 (PDF index 106), P71A and 2024 Sim donut; methods printed p.10 (PDF index 9)
added_audiobook_observations.notes: Published 19 November 2024; fieldwork 30 April to 31 July 2024, face-to-face tablet interviews in 208 municipalities. All 5504 respondents are the published base. Question asks whether an audiobook has ever been heard. Includes children age 5+. It does not measure annual listening or subscriptions. Only the observed 2024 wave is imported; earlier 2019 figures fall outside the requested period. Reviewed 16 November 2026.

added_genre_observations.denominator: Recent readers age 5+ (n=2547); at least one whole or partial book in past 3 months
added_genre_observations.population: Brazil residents age 5+; household survey, recent-reader subset
added_genre_observations.period: Book types read in the past 12 months
added_genre_observations.comparison_group: Brazil past-year book types among recent readers
added_genre_observations.evidence_locator: Printed p.47 (PDF index 46), P37 table, 2024 column; reader definition p.14; methods p.10
added_genre_observations.notes: Published 19 November 2024; fieldwork 30 April to 31 July 2024. P37 asks types of paper or digital books read in the last year, but the base is recent readers who read a whole or partial book in the last three months. Multiple answers may overlap. The 5504-person total sample is not the genre denominator. Original Portuguese categories retained; Romance means novels. Includes educational and religious book categories. No audiobook-specific genre result or market share. Outros=0 is explicitly reported and the nonresponse category remains 2. Only 2024 imported. Reviewed 16 November 2026.

added_genre_observations.notes: Published 19 November 2024; fieldwork 30 April to 31 July 2024. P37 asks types of paper or digital books read in the last year, but the base is recent readers who read a whole or partial book in the last three months. Multiple answers may overlap. The 5504-person total sample is not the genre denominator. Original Portuguese categories retained; Romance means novels. Includes educational and religious book categories. No audiobook-specific genre result or market share. Outros=0 is explicitly reported and the nonresponse category remains 2. Only 2024 imported. Reviewed 16 November 2026.
added_genre_observations.genre_scope: Book types read, paper or digital

scope_notes: Audiobook measure includes children and lifetime experience.
Genre rows combine paper and digital formats and include nonresponse.
Only observations from 2024 added. Earlier report years are outside the project window.
No reading participation by specific print or ebook format inferred from the last-book-format question.

other_reviewed_sources.decision: Hold quantitative additions. Report distinguishes reader-format43, proportion-of-books question40 and annual activity Never60. The annual activity table has answered n1006 and a conflicting All readers label despite preceding total-sample note. Exact bases remain unresolved.

No audiobook-specific usage observation verified. Reading-practice questions skip respondents deemed unable to read. Do not treat broad reading/stories or audio material definitions as audiobook listening.
